Can't be done.

A "3" in Nashville is going to be a "9" in San Francisco, or vice versa.

Even if you could find a way of averaging all the ratings out, to get something of an objective value... it's still going to be pointless, because you might average a word at a "6" rating, but that's still going to be inaccurate if the audience in the sphere where you used it would call it a "3" or a "9".

So, perhaps you could have a more specific rating system. E.g. - "on a scale of 1-10, residents of Berkeley, California who have purple hair rate this word a 17 in offensiveness," or "if you say this word near a University in Seattle, you're likely to have 26 people tell you to KYS and 14 people kill themselves." That level of specificity would make the rating system useful, even if only in highly specific circumstances... but only for a highly specific time. Who knows what is totally fine to say today, but will be totally offensive in a month? What phrase makes sense to everyone now, but will warrant a bike lock to the head next year? Who knows?

There's just no way to make such a rating system useful in the current year. Maybe after people calm down a bit in some future generation.
